ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First read the problem: the solution set of the inequality ax-b<0 is (1,+∞). Classify the linear inequality: if a>0, then ax-b<0 can be transformed into x<b/a, and the solution set should be (-∞, b/a); if a<0, then after dividing by a negative number, the inequality sign reverses, and the solution set should be x>b/a, namely (b/a,+∞). The solution set given in the problem is (1,+∞), so it must have a<0 and b/a=1, therefore b=a. Substitute b=a into the target inequality (ax+b)(x-3)>0, obtaining (ax+a)(x-3)>0, namely a(x+1)(x-3)>0. Because a<0, after dividing both sides by the negative number a, the inequality sign reverses, obtaining (x+1)(x-3)<0. The zeros of the quadratic expression are x=-1 and x=3, and when the product is less than 0, x lies between the two roots, so the solution set is (-1,3).
